previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, chronic systolic heart failure (EF 20%), BOOP, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease, was admitted with abdominal pain and bilious vomiting. He reported left flank pain radiating to the groin, consistent with a passed kidney stone, and drainage from a recurrent perirectal abscess. CT imaging confirmed mild left hydroureteronephrosis and soft tissue thickening with central hypodensity at the prior abscess site. He underwent incision and drainage with drain placement and was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later narrowed to oral Augmentin. His acute heart failure exacerbation improved with IV Lasix, and his kidney function remained stable. He was discharged to an extended care facility on home medications, including antibiotics, with follow-up planned in colorectal and orthopedic clinics.

without intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in
detecting vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor
detection.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.
Oral contrast was not administered.

 Total DLP (Body) = 887 mGy-cm.

CT abdomen pelvis on ___

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST: There are moderate to large bilateral pleural effusions and
adjacent atelectasis the heart is mildly enlarged.  There is no pericardial
effusion.

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver is normal in size and attenuation on this noncontrast
examination.  There is mild is perihepatic ascites, increased from the CT
abdomen pelvis on ___. The patient is status post cholecystectomy
with clips in the gallbladder fossa.

SPLEEN: The spleen is within normal limits.

PANCREAS: The pancreas is within normal limits on this noncontrast
examination.

ADRENALS: The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

URINARY: The kidneys are somewhat atrophic.  There is mild hydronephrosis in
the left kidney.  The right kidney shows no evidence of hydronephrosis.

GASTROINTESTINAL: The stomach is within normal limits.  Multiple loops of
small bowel are normal appearing without evidence of obstruction.  The colon
is normal in caliber.  There is scattered diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon
without evidence of diverticulitis.  The appendix is normal.

size criteria.

VASCULAR: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber.  There is mild
atherosclerotic disease.

limits.  There is no pelvic lymphadenopathy.

in the visualized osseous structures.

1. Small to moderate perihepatic ascites is increased from the prior

or pelvis.  No evidence of colitis.  Normal appendix.  No evidence of bowel
obstruction.
